A family is going hungry
Carts cannot reach the logging plot and return in daylight. Mark out a closer plot or wait for longer days.
Logging plot too far
When hauling in winter, bring home the floodplain haystacks first.

Flood threatens hay
At year-end, repay the loan out of what is left after plan deliveries and seed are covered. Unpaid debt carries over with a surcharge of one fifth, or less if your reputation is good.
District loan unpaid
Haul the crop in. It will be picked up automatically once storage space is available. Until then it stays out in the open.
Harvest still in the field
The field is ripe and short of harvest workers. Snow will take what is left. Call an all-hands rush for the harvest by pulling people off other work.
Harvest at risk before snow
Set up a straw stack before harvest.
Before harvest, build a granary for grain or set up a storage clamp by the field for potatoes and vegetables.
Harvest won't fit in storage
The horses are getting old and there are no foals. The summer yard needs a roof for breeding. Upgrade the horse yard to a stable or buy horses from the district before you run short of plow horses.
Horses aging without a stable
Upgrade the livestock yard to an Insulated livestock yard before frost.
First frost in {days} {days}|plural(one=day,other=days). No warm shelter for {heads} {heads}|plural(one=animal,other=animals).
Some of the herd will have no warm shelter when frost comes. Upgrade to an Insulated livestock yard. Pause other construction if it is pulling workers away.
Not enough warm shelter
Upgrade to an Insulated livestock yard. You can build it in winter.
Out in the cold: {heads} {heads}|plural(one=animal,other=animals).
Cold reduces milk yield and pulling power. Livestock left in the cold yard will start dying. Upgrade to an Insulated livestock yard. You can build it in winter.
Herd is freezing
End all-hands rush

Assign people to Harvesting in the meadows.
Today is a dry day off. You can make it a workday for haymaking, at the cost of people's rest.
You can make {weekday} a workday for haymaking if the morning is dry. People will lose their day off.
Build a granary for compound feed. The district will only accept an allocation order if there is room to store it.
The all-hands rush on haymaking has lasted four days. You can end it.
The forecast still shows a shortage with the feed due to arrive.
Haymaking is underway. A hay shortage is still forecast. There is no further haymaking advice for today.
Send {heads} {heads}|plural(one=animal,other=animals) to the district to cut feed use. The oldest animals go. For horses, it is working animals that go.

After haymaking, in {days} {days}|plural(one=day,other=days), you can send {heads} {heads}|plural(one=animal,other=animals) to the district. The oldest animals go. For horses, it is working animals that go.
After haymaking, on {weekday}, you can send {heads} {heads}|plural(one=animal,other=animals) to the district. The oldest animals go. For horses, it is working animals that go.
The forecast shows a short spell of underfeeding, with no deaths expected. You can hold off on buying feed or sending animals away.
Hay first runs short in {days} {days}|plural(one=day,other=days). The shortage before fresh-cut hay comes in is {tonnes} t.
Livestock short of hay before grazing: {heads}. Compound feed and straw cannot cover the gap.
Hay will last {days} {days}|plural(one=day,other=days), until {month}. The shortage before fresh-cut hay comes in is {tonnes} t.
Feed may run short
Bring in suitable feed or send part of the herd to the district.
Open the reserve. It holds feed suitable for the herd.
Bring in feed or reduce the herd. Underfed livestock give no milk and do not breed.
Herd is underfed
The herd is aging. The stallion needs shelter for breeding. Before year three, upgrade the horse yard to tier two, a stable. A groom can tend the horses, but they still need a roof.
Herd shrinking without a stable
A house is about to collapse and the family has nowhere to move. Start building a house at the suggested site.
People are ready to move here and need somewhere to live. Build barracks for newcomers.
A wedding is waiting on housing. Start building houses at the suggested sites.
{homes} {homes}|plural(one=house,other=houses) needed.
{barrack_places} {barrack_places}|plural(one=place,other=places) needed in the barracks.
Needed: {homes} {homes}|plural(one=house,other=houses) and {barrack_places} {barrack_places}|plural(one=place,other=places) in the barracks.
A housing shortage delays weddings, keeps newcomers away and leaves families in unsafe houses. Start building houses at the suggested sites and build barracks for newcomers.
Not enough housing

Grass uncut before snow

All morning milk goes to the district against the debt. None is left for households. Check the year book. Protect the herd and improve feeding to raise milk yield. You can discuss the plan item with the district.
Milk goes to repay debt
Cover the shortfall on this plan item by year-end. Set aside produce for the district's next collection.
Plan item short

Put the crop in rotation on your best fields this year. Sow at least the area the district expects for this plan item. The alert clears when there is enough land. Check the field itself for its expected yield.
Too little land for the plan
The crew cannot walk to the planting area and back in daylight. Plant closer to housing or wait for longer days.
Planting area too far
Open the idle workshop to see what it needs. Restore its inputs, workers or room for finished products, depending on what stopped work.
Processing has stopped
People are close to going hungry while grain sits in reserve. You can open the reserve. Any seed eaten now will be missing at spring sowing.
Food locked in reserves
{crop}: not enough seed for {hectares} {hectares}|plural(one=hectare,other=hectares). We will sow less.
The seed loan has already been issued. The district will lend no more this season. Set aside more seed in autumn for next time or plan fewer fields for this crop.
Seed shortage cuts sowing
Next season's seed is still in the field and other crops have filled storage. Grain needs a granary. Potatoes need a vegetable storehouse or storage clamp. Build or clear space before harvest ends.
No room for seed
Seed is short for the next sowing. Choose “Take a seed loan” or adjust the rotation to your stock. Repay one fifth extra, or less if your reputation is good. Unpaid debt grows each year.
Not enough seed
Move deliveries to this site ahead of fieldwork. That leaves fewer carts for the fields.
Materials are in storage. Site: {unit}. Working days without a delivery: {amount}.
Site awaiting delivery
Workers cannot currently get from the nearest house to the site and back in daylight. If you cannot wait for longer days, choose a site closer to housing.
Building site too far
Assign workers to the site and keep them there while construction is underway. They do not come on their own. The alert tracks who is on site now, even if you assigned them yesterday.
Building crew needed
Order the missing materials with your district allocation or change the construction supply queue. Work starts when materials arrive.
Check the sawmill in the service yard and its stock of logs. The sawmill cuts them into boards.
In Epoch I, only the bricks already in storage are available. From Epoch II, you can order more with your allocation.
Mark out a pit for clay and a shoal for sand.
Order this material with your district allocation.
This material is unavailable in this epoch. The site cannot be finished yet.
Mark out a logging plot and assign people to cut logs.
Mark out a quarry. Stone is piled by the ruins of the count's manor.
Straw will be available after reaping. Construction has to wait until then.
Building materials short
Slaughter starts once there is room for the meat. Clear space in a food store or an icehouse.
Slaughter needs storage
More land is plowed than the crew can sow in time for the crop to ripen before snow. Put people and horses on sowing or leave the field fallow.
Sowing will run late
{days} {days}|plural(one=day,other=days) until the sowing deadline.
Keep plowing, harrowing and sowing on schedule. Late sowing reduces the yield.
Sowing window closing
Upgrade the store or build a second one. Until then the harvest stays in the field.
Storage is full
Without oats, horses plow and harrow less effectively. Open the reserve if oats are set aside there. Plan more oats in next year's rotation. Use “Change priority” to move deliveries up the queue.
Horses out of oats
There are not enough horses for the teams, so people pull the loads themselves. Buy a horse with the district allocation or cancel some assignments.
Not enough horses

Put an early crop or fallow before the winter crop. Normally sow in August or September the year before harvest. A warm October still allows sowing at a lower yield. After October, the field stays fallow.
Winter crop after late harvest
Horses are kept in household yards and people spend time caring for them. Assign a groom to the horse yard to bring the herd together and free people for their own work.
Horse yard needs a groom
